title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-10-07
body:
Summary:
This week focused on three coordinated efforts: kernel-level attention optimizations, KV cache correctness and TTL work, and batching pipeline improvements. Progress was steady; we merged two PRs that together improve end-to-end p95 for short chat requests and increase steady-state throughput for medium-length sequences.

Highlights:
- Kernel optimizations: merged PR #3421 (fused-attn micro-optimizations). On A100, microbenchmarks show ~12% per-token execution time reduction for causal attention with sequence lengths <= 256. Reduced kernel launch overhead by batching smaller GEMM calls.
- KV cache: fixed a race in cache invalidation (ENG-4821) that caused stale KV entries on model reload. Also tightened TTL semantics so cached prefixes expire predictably across shards; observed 18% reduction in cold-start token penalty during canary runs.
- Batching: updated the batching policy heuristics (PR #3468) to bias by recent request latency profiles and model size. For our standard chat workload (seq 32-128) steady-state throughput increased ~20% while keeping p95 within SLO.

Quantitative metrics (canary cluster - dedicated pool, Oct 6 run):
- Short chat generation (32 tokens): p95 latency 310ms -> 270ms (12.9% improvement).
- Medium chat (128 tokens): throughput 820 reqs/min -> 980 reqs/min (19.5% improvement).
- Cold-start token penalty (first request after reload): median 420ms -> 345ms (17.9% improvement).
- CPU overhead for routing service: +3% (acceptable for current capacity).

Standup notes (week of 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-09):
- Mon 2026-10-05: Kernel team: landed fused-attn micro-ops; started cross-check with quantization branch. KV team: repro of TTL inconsistency confirmed (ENG-4821). Batching: collected latency histograms to feed adaptive policy.
- Tue 2026-10-06: Integration testing for kernel + quantization (smoke tests pass on x86 with int8 fallback). KV team validated patch on staging; observed inconsistent invalidation on shard boundary.
- Wed 2026-10-07: Canary rollout of fused-attn to 10% traffic. Observed improved p50/p95 but one customer scenario showed tokenization-induced long sequences causing higher-than-expected memory.
- Thu 2026-10-08: KV TTL fix rolled to canary; race fixed by single-writer per-shard guard and stronger reload fence. Batching heuristics adjusted to cap max batch size for large models.
- Fri 2026-10-09: Full-mesh canary (all internal tests) green; preparing gradual rollout to prod-dedicated next week.

Cross-team meeting notes (with infra & SRE on 2026-10-07):
- SRE asked for clearer rollback signals for kernel changes; we agreed to ship a metric (kernel-failure-rate) and an auto-fallback to previous kernel variant if failure_rate > 0.5% over 5m.
- Infra requested cap on GPU memory per-request for canary to avoid OOMs from tokenization spikes; we added a soft limit and early-reject path with 429.
- Decided to coordinate rollout windows with Dedicated customers in CET mornings to minimize impact.

Blockers / Risks:
- Quantization compatibility: the fused-attn changes need one more refactor to avoid regressing int8 speed on T4-class GPUs (ticket ENG-4897). Estimated 3 engineering days.
- A small subset of large-sequence customers still see memory pressure under the new batching policy; need per-customer tuning before 100% rollout.

Action items:
- Marco: finish refactor for quantization compatibility (ENG-4897) by 2026-10-12.
- Lina: instrument and publish kernel-failure-rate metric and wire into rollback runbook by 2026-10-09.
- Owen: run customer smoke tests for two large-seq customers and produce tuning recommendations by 2026-10-13.
- Aisha: prepare rollout plan for Dedicated pool (staged: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%) and schedule canary-to-prod window with SRE for 2026-10-14.

Notes / Open questions:
- Need decision on whether to keep the new batching heuristic as default for hosted-api (we currently plan to gate by customer tier).
- Should we expose the KV TTL setting as a per-tenant knob? Pros: flexibility for heavy prefix workloads. Cons: complexity and support burden.

Attachments / Links:
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/3421, https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/3468
- JIRA: ENG-4821 (KV TTL race), ENG-4897 (quantization compat refactor)
- Confluence runbook (draft): /pages/serving-runtime/kernel-kv-batching

Summary/Next week:
Focus will be finishing the quantization refactor, stabilizing the batching policy for large-seq customers, and executing the staged Dedicated rollout. Goal is to have the gates and rollback metrics in place before moving beyond 30% traffic.

Drafted by: Aisha Patel
Reviewers: Marco Rivera, Lina Chen, Owen Gallagher
